case_name: Hridaya Ranjan Prasad Verma & Others v. State of Bihar & Another

pages.text:
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
Hridaya Ranjan Prasad Verma and Others ... Appellants
versus
State of Bihar and Another ... Respondents
Coram: D.P. Wadhwa, S.S.M. Quadri, JJ.
Judgment Dated: 31 March 2000

QUADRI, J.:
1. This appeal deals with the boundary between a civil breach of contract and criminal cheating under Section 415 and Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

2. Distinction Between Breach of Contract and Cheating: In breach of contract, the failure to perform may be due to subsequent contingencies or inability. In cheating, there must be a fraudulent or dishonest intention right at the beginning (inception) of the transaction. Mere inability of the promisor to deliver or honour a cheque at a later date does not constitute criminal cheating unless fraudulent intention existed ab initio.

3. Decision: In the absence of an allegation that the appellants had no intention to execute the sale deed or honour the contract at the inception, the dispute is purely civil. Criminal proceedings under Section 420 IPC quashed.
